meta.title: Engineering systems with a reason to exist.
meta.description: Projects turn research and technical practice into working systems. Each one is documented as part of a larger engineering trajectory, not as an isolated showcase.

featured.name: Nordic Green Data Platform
featured.description: A data engineering platform designed to acquire, structure and expose Nordic environmental and energy data through a dependable, extensible pipeline.
featured.objective: Turn complex source data into transparent, analytics-ready datasets while building a foundation for cloud delivery and future intelligent systems.

flow.name: Acquire
flow.description: Collect environmental and energy datasets from reliable sources.

flow.name: Transform
flow.description: Normalize structures and make data quality decisions explicit.

flow.name: Store
flow.description: Persist dependable datasets for repeatable analysis.

flow.name: Explore
flow.description: Expose useful signals through analytics and interfaces.

milestones.title: Pipeline foundation
milestones.description: Strengthen ingestion, transformation and storage as one traceable data flow.

milestones.title: Interactive dashboard
milestones.description: Turn prepared datasets into an accessible analytical experience.

milestones.title: Cloud & AI integration
milestones.description: Expand only after the data and software foundations are dependable.

registry.title: A registry of practical engineering work.
registry.description: The current catalog is intentionally focused. Every system must demonstrate a useful capability and contribute knowledge to the broader NEXUS ecosystem.

systems.name: HEVY Pipeline
systems.summary: A focused data pipeline for extracting structured workout data from APIs, transforming it with Python and Pandas, and preparing useful analytical datasets in SQLite.

systems.name: NEXUS
systems.summary: The evolving application that connects projects, research and technical progression through a modular, data-driven interface built for long-term growth.
